Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a truly memorable event. With 
inspiration from the then U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, and 
soaring arias from the magnificent Andrea Bocelli and Maria Alcida, 
plus mind boggling magic from Lior Suchard, all sewn together by 
our emcee David Walliams, it was one of the happiest evenings 
we can remember at our home. 
This year's Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the generous support of our friends 
at BVLGARI, promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary performer Joan Baez, who has not only created 
her own iconic classics, but has fabulously reinterpreted music by 
everyone from Bob Dylan and Stevie Wonder to the Rolling Stones, 
Ryan Adams and Josh Ritter, will perform for us. Elton is looking 
forward to sharing a stage with her for the first time ever. The 
wonderful David Walliams will look after us as emcee and we have 
some very special VIP guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the Woodside Gallery Dinner do so much 
good. You may remember a young man named Leslie who spoke at 
last year's event. When he was a child, Leslie's grandmother died of 
AIDS. He was at her bedside. Today, Leslie works to educate the 
LGBT community in South Africa about HIV. He travels to 
townships and slums, providing HIV testing and referring those who 
need it to clinics where they will not be shamed or turned away. 
Thanks to your generosity, this work has expanded to 200 clinics 
nationally. We visited one in July with the South African Minister of 
Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us that the success of these 
services in preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS is helping the South 
African government to now afford funding all medical HIV treatment 
for its people without external support. 
EFTA_R1_00942666 
EFTA02215007
--- PAGE 4 ---
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince Harry onstage at the International AIDS 
Conference in Durban to talk about the critical need to 
help adolescents living with HIV. We urged the international 
community not to give up on this precious group when we have had 
so much success fighting the epidemic amongst adults, mothers and 
babies. Reaching adolescents is our last huge global challenge in the 
fight against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues that call for our attention today. I cannot tell you 
how grateful David and I and everyone at the Foundation arc that 
you continue to share our passion and our vision for a future where 
AIDS is not something our children or our grandchildren will have to 
worry about. Healthy societies, at home and abroad, mean less 
instability or dependence on others. We believe it is not only 
possible but essential. 
We do hope you will join us in June so we can continue the work of the Foundation. 
You can download your invitation to purchase tickets to this year's 
Woodside Gallery Dinner below. 
With your support, we will fight the stigma, stop new infections and save countless 
lives. 
In the meantime, if you need any further information on the Woodside Gallery 
Dinner, please do not hesitate to contact Glenn Horder at the 
Foundation as per contact details below. 
With our warmest regards,

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish at Home 
for the Elton John AIDS Foundation 
THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a truly 
memorable event. With inspiration from the then U.S. 
Secretary of State John Kerry, and soaring arias from the 
magnificent Andrea Bocelli and Maria Aleida, plus mind 
boggling magic from Lior Suchard, all sewn together by our 
emcee David Walliams, it was one of the happiest evenings 
we can remember at our home. 
EFTA_R1_00944307 
EFTA02215906
--- PAGE 4 ---
This year's Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the generous 
support of our friends at BVLGARI, promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary performer Joan Baez, who 
has not only created her own iconic classics, but has 
fabulously reinterpreted music by everyone from Bob Dylan 
and Stevie Wonder to the Rolling Stones, Ryan Adams and 
Josh Ritter, will perform for us. Elton is looking forward to 
sharing a stage with her for the first time ever. The 
wonderful David Walliams will look after us as emcee and we 
have some very special VIP guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the Woodside 
Gallery Dinner do so much good. You may remember a young 
man named Leslie who spoke at last year's event. When he 
was a child, Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. He was at her 
bedside. Today, Leslie works to educate the LGBT community 
in South Africa about HIV. He travels to townships and slums, 
providing HIV testing and referring those who need it to 
clinics where they will not be shamed or turned away. 
Thanks to your generosity, this work has expanded to 200 
clinics nationally. We visited one in July with the South 
African Minister of Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us 
that the success of these services in preventing the spread of 
HIV/AIDS is helping the South African government to 
now afford funding all medical HIV treatment for its 
people without external support. 
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince Harry onstage at the 
International AIDS Conference in Durban to talk about the 
critical need to help adolescents living with HIV. We urged 
the international community not to give up on this precious 
group when we have had so much success fighting the 
epidemic amongst adults, mothers and babies. Reaching 
adolescents is our last huge global challenge in the fight 
against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues that call for our attention 
today. I cannot tell you how grateful David and I and 
everyone at the Foundation are that you continue to share 
our passion and our vision for a future where AIDS is not 
something our children or our grandchildren will have to 
worry about. Healthy societies, at home and abroad, mean 
less instability or dependence on others. We believe it is not 
only possible but essential. 
We do hope you will join us in June so we can continue the

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish at Home 
for the Elton John AIDS Foundation 
THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a truly memorable event. With 
inspiration from the then U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, and soaring 
arias from the magnificent Andrea Bocelli and Maria Aleida, plus mind 
boggling magic from Lior Suchard, all sewn together by our emcee David 
Walliams, it was one of the happiest evenings we can remember at our 
home. 
This year's Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the generous support of our 
friends at BVLGARI, promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary performer Joan Baez, who has not only 
created her own iconic classics, but has fabulously reinterpreted music by 
everyone from Bob Dylan and Stevie Wonder to the Rolling Stones, Ryan 
Adams and Josh Ritter, will perform for us. Elton is looking forward to 
sharing a stage with her for the first time ever. The wonderful David 
Walliams will look after us as emcee and we have some very special VIP 
guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the Woodside Gallery Dinner do 
so much good. You may remember a young man named Leslie who spoke 
at last year's event. When he was a child, Leslie's grandmother died of 
AIDS. He was at her bedside. Today, Leslie works to educate the 
LGBT community in South Africa about HIV. He travels to townships and 
slums, providing HIV testing and referring those who need it to clinics 
EFTA_R1_00944499 
EFTA02215998
--- PAGE 3 ---
where they will not be shamed or turned away. Thanks to your generosity, 
this work has expanded to 200 clinics nationally. We visited one in July 
with the South African Minister of Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us 
that the success of these services in preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS is 
helping the South African government to now afford funding all medical 
HIV treatment for its people without external support. 
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince Harry onstage at the International AIDS 
Conference in Durban to talk about the critical need to help adolescents 
living with HIV. We urged the international community not to give up on 
this precious group when we have had so much success fighting the 
epidemic amongst adults, mothers and babies. Reaching adolescents is our 
last huge global challenge in the fight against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues that call for our attention today. I 
cannot tell you how grateful David and I and everyone at the Foundation 
are that you continue to share our passion and our vision for a future 
where AIDS is not something our children or our grandchildren will have to 
worry about. Healthy societies, at home and abroad, mean less instability 
or dependence on others. We believe it is not only possible but essential. 
We do hope you will join us in June so we can continue the work of the 
Foundation. You can download your invitation to purchase tickets to this 
year's Woodside Gallery Dinner below. 
With your support, we will fight the stigma, stop new infections and save 
countless lives. 
In the meantime, if you need any further information on the Woodside 
Gallery Dinner, please do not hesitate to contact Glenn Horder at the 
Foundation as per contact details below. 
With our warmest regards, 
Founder 
Elton John 
Chairman 
David Furnish

In addition to dedicated locations where you can take advantage

The wonderful David

As well as being fabulous fun, 
events like the Woodside Gallery 
Dinner do so much good. You may 
remember a young man named 
Leslie who spoke at last year's 
event. When he was a child, 
Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. 
He was at her bedside. Today, 
Leslie works to educate the 
LGBT community in South Africa 
about HIV. He travels to 
townships and slums, 
providing HIV testing and referring 
those who need it to clinics where 
they will not be shamed or turned 
away. Thanks to your generosity, 
this work has expanded to 200 
clinics nationally. We visited one 
in July with the South African 
Minister of Health, Aaron 
Motsoaledi, who told us that the 
success of these services in 
preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS 
is helping the South African 
government to now afford funding 
all medical HIV treatment for its 
people without external support. 
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince 
Harry onstage at the International 
AIDS Conference in Durban to talk 
about the critical need to 
help adolescents living with HIV. 
We urged the international 
community not to give up on this 
precious group when we have had 
so much success fighting the 
epidemic amongst adults, mothers 
and babies. Reaching adolescents 
is our last huge global challenge in 
the fight against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish at Home 
for the Elton John AIDS Foundation 
THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United Kingdom 
Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last year was a 
truly memorable event. With inspiration from 
the then U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, and 
soaring arias from the magnificent Andrea 
EFTA_R1_00945386 
EFTA02216307
--- PAGE 4 ---
Bocelli and Maria Aleida, plus mind boggling 
magic from Lior Suchard, all sewn together by 
our emcee David Walliams, it was one of the 
happiest evenings we can remember at our 
home. 
This year's Woodside Gallery Dinner, with the 
generous support of our friends at BVLGARI, 
promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary 
performer Joan Baez, who has not only created 
her own iconic classics, but has 
fabulously reinterpreted music by everyone 
from Bob Dylan and Stevie Wonder to the 
Rolling Stones, Ryan Adams and Josh Ritter, will 
perform for us. Elton is looking forward to 
sharing a stage with her for the first time ever. 
The wonderful David Walliams will look after us 
as emcee and we have some very special VIP 
guests confirmed. 
As well as being fabulous fun, events like the 
Woodside Gallery Dinner do so much good. You 
may remember a young man named Leslie who 
spoke at last year's event. When he was a child, 
Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. He was at 
her bedside. Today, Leslie works to educate the 
LGBT community in South Africa about HIV. He 
travels to townships and slums, providing HIV 
testing and referring those who need it to clinics 
where they will not be shamed or turned away. 
Thanks to your generosity, this work has 
expanded to 200 clinics nationally. We visited 
one in July with the South African Minister of 
Health, Aaron Motsoaledi, who told us that the 
success of these services in preventing the 
spread of HIV/AIDS is helping the South African 
government to now afford funding all medical 
HIV treatment for its people without external 
support. 
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince Harry onstage 
at the International AIDS Conference in Durban 
to talk about the critical need to 
help adolescents living with HIV. We urged the 
international community not to give up on this 
precious group when we have had so much 
EFTA_R1_00945387 
EFTA02216308
--- PAGE 5 ---
success fighting the epidemic amongst adults, 
mothers and babies. Reaching adolescents is 
our last huge global challenge in the fight 
against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues that call for 
our attention today. I cannot tell you how 
grateful David and I and everyone at the 
Foundation are that you continue to share our 
passion and our vision for a future where AIDS 
is not something our children or our 
grandchildren will have to worry about. 
Healthy societies, at home and abroad, mean 
less instability or dependence on others. We 
believe it is not only possible but essential. 
We do hope you will join us in June so we can 
continue the work of the Foundation. You can 
download your invitation to purchase tickets to 
this year's Woodside Gallery Dinner below. 
With your support, we will fight the stigma, stop 
new infections and save countless lives. 
In the meantime, if you need any further 
information on the Woodside Gallery Dinner, 
please do not hesitate to contact Glenn Horder 
at the Foundation as per contact details below. 
With our warmest regards, 
Elton John 
David Furnish

Dear Peggy, 
Sir Elton John and David Furnish 
at Home

THURSDAY 22nd JUNE 2017 
Woodside Gallery, Woodside, 
Crimp Hill 
Old Windsor, Berkshire, United

Our Woodside Gallery Dinner last 
year was a truly memorable event. 
With inspiration from the then 
U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry, 
and soaring arias from the 
magnificent Andrea Bocelli and 
Maria Aleida, plus mind boggling 
magic from Lior Suchard, all sewn 
together by our emcee David 
Walliams, it was one of the 
happiest evenings we can 
remember at our home. 
This year's Woodside Gallery 
Dinner, with the generous support 
of our friends at BVLGARI, 
promises to be as magical. 
We are so excited that legendary 
performer Joan Baez, who has not 
only created her own iconic 
classics, but has 
fabulously reinterpreted music by 
everyone from Bob Dylan and 
Stevie Wonder to the Rolling 
Stones, Ryan Adams and Josh

looking forward to sharing a stage 
with her for the first time ever.

Walliams will look after us as 
emcee and we have some very 
special VIP guests confirmed. 
EFTA_R1_00945531 
EFTA02216398
--- PAGE 5 ---
As well as being fabulous fun, 
events like the Woodside Gallery 
Dinner do so much good. You may 
remember a young man named 
Leslie who spoke at last year's 
event. When he was a child, 
Leslie's grandmother died of AIDS. 
He was at her bedside. Today, 
Leslie works to educate the 
LGBT community in South Africa 
about HIV. He travels to 
townships and slums, 
providing HIV testing and referring 
those who need it to clinics where 
they will not be shamed or turned 
away. Thanks to your generosity, 
this work has expanded to 200 
clinics nationally. We visited one 
in July with the South African 
Minister of Health, Aaron 
Motsoaledi, who told us that the 
success of these services in 
preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS 
is helping the South African 
government to now afford funding 
all medical HIV treatment for its 
people without external support. 
Also last July, I joined HRH Prince 
Harry onstage at the International 
AIDS Conference in Durban to talk 
about the critical need to 
help adolescents living with HIV. 
We urged the international 
community not to give up on this 
precious group when we have had 
so much success fighting the 
epidemic amongst adults, mothers 
and babies. Reaching adolescents 
is our last huge global challenge in 
the fight against AIDS. 
There are so many pressing issues 
that call for our attention today. I 
cannot tell you how grateful David 
and I and everyone at the 
Foundation are that you continue
